patients.summary: Healthy construction project coordinator who joins the practice at 26. In July 2025 he has Guillain-Barre syndrome (AIDP) treated with IVIG and recovers; a year later he has a recurrence as the Miller Fisher variant (anti-GQ1b positive) and is recovering as of today.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26M here to set up primary care. Wants a practice closer to home; records release signed today.

No complaints. Feels well. No meds, no supplements. NKDA. No surgeries, no hospital stays.

FHx: father with high blood pressure, on treatment and well controlled. Mother hypothyroid. Nobody in the immediate family with autoimmune disease or nerve/muscle disorders that he knows of.

Social: works as a project coordinator for a construction firm, splits time between the office and job sites. Lives alone in South Hadley. Never smoked, no vaping. Couple of beers a week, sometimes three. No drug use.

ROS: negative across the board. Sleeps fine, mood good.

Exam: well-appearing young man, comfortable. Vitals as charted, BP normal. HEENT clear, TMs normal, oropharynx normal. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged, no adenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Skin: no concerning lesions. Neuro: strength and gait normal, reflexes 2+ and symmetric.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
1. Health maintenance, healthy adult. Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HIV and HCV screening, he agrees. Tdap today, last one he can recall was in high school. Flu and COVID once the fall supply is in, will set up a nurse visit.
2. Records requested from prior PCP.

Return in a year for a physical.

Interval: nothing new since last fall. No ER or urgent care visits. Busy season at work, lots of hours on job sites, otherwise good. Still no meds.

Habits unchanged: never smoker, a few drinks a week, no drugs. Wears hearing protection and steel toes on site. Seat belt always.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD (received by fax 07/21/2025)
Date of visit: 07/11/2025

CC: legs weak, feet tingling

HPI: 28-year-old man, healthy, no daily medications. Three days ago both feet began to feel like pins and needles. Over the next two days his legs got progressively weaker. This morning he could not get up from the couch without pushing off with his arms and needed the railing for every step. Today he has also had trouble holding onto his coffee mug and turning his truck key. Denies back pain, bowel or bladder change, shortness of breath, trouble swallowing, double vision or facial droop. No recent vaccines. No tick bites he knows of.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father hypertensive, controlled. Mother on thyroid replacement. No autoimmune or neuromuscular disease in parents or siblings.
Social: construction project coordinator. Never smoker. 2-3 drinks/week.

Exam: vitals within normal limits. Alert, conversant, speech clear. Cranial nerves II-XII intact; extraocular movements full, face symmetric, palate and tongue midline. Motor: weakness in both legs, symmetric, involving hip flexors and extensors as well as ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion. Intrinsic hand muscles mildly weak on both sides. Reflexes absent at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, knees and ankles. Toes downgoing. Sensation to light touch, pinprick, vibration and position intact in all four limbs. Lungs clear, speaking full sentences, good cough. Abdomen benign. No spinal tenderness.

ED course: CBC, CMP and CK unremarkable. Neurology consulted at bedside; agrees presentation is most consistent with Guillain-Barre syndrome. Lumbar puncture and respiratory monitoring per neurology on the floor.

Impression: acute ascending symmetric weakness with areflexia, Guillain-Barre syndrome.
Disposition: admitted to neurology.

medications.drug_text: human immunoglobulin G 100 MG/ML Injectable Solution
medications.sig: 0.4 g/kg IV once daily for 5 days (2 g/kg total)

reports.text: Motor nerve conduction studies of the bilateral median, ulnar, peroneal and tibial nerves show prolonged distal motor latencies and slowed conduction velocities, with temporal dispersion of the compound muscle action potentials. F-wave latencies are prolonged or absent in all nerves tested. Sensory studies of the median, ulnar and sural nerves show normal amplitudes. Needle EMG of selected arm and leg muscles shows reduced recruitment without spontaneous activity.
reports.conclusion: Electrodiagnostic findings consistent with an acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy, involving arms and legs.

procedures.procedure: Nerve conduction study with needle EMG
Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Neurology Discharge Summary
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - Neurology inpatient service (received 07/21/2025)
Admitted 07/11/2025, discharged 07/18/2025

Principal diagnosis: Guillain-Barre syndrome, acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (AIDP).
Allergies: NKDA.

Presentation: 28M with three days of distal paresthesias followed by symmetric proximal and distal leg weakness and mild hand weakness, areflexic, sensory exam normal, cranial nerves spared. See ED record.

Hospital course:
- LP 07/11: CSF protein 96 mg/dL, glucose 61 mg/dL, WBC 2/uL, RBC 0/uL. Albuminocytologic dissociation.
- IVIG 0.4 g/kg daily x5 days, 07/12 through 07/16, 2 g/kg total. Tolerated without reaction.
- NCS/EMG 07/14: demyelinating pattern in arms and legs, consistent with AIDP.
- Respiratory: FVC and NIF checked every 8 hours. FVC never fell below 3.8 L and NIF stayed at -60 cmH2O or stronger. No ICU transfer needed.
- Weakness reached its worst on hospital day 4 (07/14) and stopped progressing; slow gains after that.
- PT/OT: ambulating household distances with a rolling walker by discharge, stairs with rail and standby assist.

Condition at discharge: stable, improving. Walking with rolling walker.
Discharge medications: none.
DME: rolling walker.
Follow-up: neurology clinic in about 4-6 weeks. Outpatient physical therapy referral sent. PCP within 1-2 weeks.
Return if new trouble breathing or swallowing, facial weakness, or weakness getting worse again.
Work: off until cleared by neurology.

documents.title: In the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just so you know I got admitted Friday. My legs gave out pretty much and they're saying it's Guillain-Barre. They started IV immunoglobulin Saturday. Not sure how long I'll be here. I'll need a note for work at some point. Thanks.

documents.title: RE: In the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Tyler, thanks for letting us know, and I'm sorry you're dealing with this. You're in the right place, and IVIG is the standard treatment. Focus on getting through the hospital stay; neurology will tell you when it's safe to go back to work and we can handle the paperwork. Once you're discharged our nurse will call you and we'll get you in within a week or so.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Phone Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Called pt after discharge 7/18 (neurology admission, GBS, got IVIG). Hospital records came in yesterday, in chart.

Pt says he is home, using the walker in the apartment and to the car. Legs a little stronger each day. Breathing fine, swallowing fine, no new numbness. No meds to reconcile, none prescribed at discharge. First outpatient PT visit is Thursday afternoon. Friend is driving him.

Reviewed when to go straight to the ED: any trouble breathing or swallowing, face weakness, or legs getting weaker again. Pt verbalized understanding.

Appt with PCP Thursday 7/24 at 9:20 confirmed.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital visit.

28M admitted 7/11-7/18 to neurology at the regional hospital with Guillain-Barre syndrome (AIDP on NCS 7/14, CSF protein 96 with WBC 2). Received IVIG 2 g/kg over 5 days. Respiratory numbers held up the whole stay, no ICU. Hospital records reviewed in full.

Since discharge: improving bit by bit. Uses the rolling walker for anything past the kitchen. Getting off the toilet and out of a chair is easier than in the hospital. Grip better, still clumsy with small buttons. No breathing or swallowing complaints. No new sensory symptoms. Sleeping OK. Mood a bit frustrated about being off work but fine overall.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: vitals normal. Comfortable, came back with walker. Speech normal, face symmetric, EOM full. Strength: hip flexors 4/5 both sides, ankle dorsiflexion 4+/5 both sides, grip slightly weak both hands. Reflexes absent throughout. Sensation intact to light touch and pinprick. Lungs clear, counts to 20 on one breath without difficulty. Heart regular.

A/P
1. Guillain-Barre syndrome, AIDP, after IVIG, recovering as expected. Continue outpatient PT. Neurology visit in August. Reviewed the warning signs again. Walker until PT says otherwise.
2. Work: out of work note through his neurology appointment; neurology to clear return.

Call or message any time if things slip. Recheck as needed, otherwise physical in the fall.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:

Tyler Griffin is under my care following a hospital stay from July 11 to July 18, 2025. He is unable to work at this time while he recovers and attends physical therapy. I expect to update this after his specialist visit in late August.

Primary Care Physician

documents.title: Neurology Clinic Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology outpatient clinic
Visit date: 08/20/2025

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Griffin, 28, in follow-up after his admission last month for Guillain-Barre syndrome (AIDP), treated with a 5-day course of IVIG.

He is doing well. He stopped using the walker about ten days ago and is walking around the neighborhood daily. Stairs are fine with a hand on the rail. He has been going to PT twice a week. Hands back to normal for most tasks. No breathing or swallowing symptoms. No medications. NKDA.

Exam: alert, cranial nerves normal. Strength 5-/5 at the hip flexors bilaterally, 5/5 elsewhere in arms and legs. Reflexes remain absent. Sensation intact. Gait normal-based and steady, can walk on heels and toes.

Impression: Guillain-Barre syndrome, AIDP subtype, recovering well after IVIG.

Plan:
- He may return to work on 09/02/2025, starting with office duties and moving to job sites as he tolerates.
- Continue PT until discharged by the therapist.
- His illness did not follow any vaccination, so I see no reason he should avoid routine vaccines, including this season's flu shot.
- I will see him again in the new year.

Thank you for allowing me to share in his care.

Neurology

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual physical, 28M.

Interval history: GBS in July (AIDP, IVIG, 1-week admission). Saw neurology 8/20, doing well. Back to work since 9/2, desk the first two weeks and now back out on sites. Walking, stairs and ladders all OK. Still a couple of PT sessions left. No numbness, no weakness he notices.

Meds: none. NKDA. Never smoker, a few drinks a week.

PHQ-9 2, a rough summer but mood is good.

Exam: vitals fine. HEENT normal. Neck without nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Neuro: CN intact, strength 5/5 throughout including hip flexors, can rise from a squat without hands. Reflexes reduced, trace at biceps, not obtained at knees or ankles. Sensation intact. Gait normal.

A/P
1. Guillain-Barre syndrome, recovering. Neurology follow-up in January.
2. Health maintenance. Flu vaccine given today. He asked whether it's safe after GBS; reviewed neurology's letter, which says his illness was not vaccine-related and routine vaccines are fine. He wants to skip COVID this year. Labs from 2023 normal, nothing due.

Physical next fall.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology outpatient clinic
Visit date: 01/20/2026

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Griffin returned six months after his episode of Guillain-Barre syndrome (AIDP, July 2025, IVIG).

He reports he is back to his usual self. Full duty at work since the fall, including job sites. Finished physical therapy in November. No weakness, numbness, falls or breathing symptoms.

Exam: cranial nerves normal. Strength 5/5 throughout. Reflexes trace in the arms, absent at the knees and ankles. Sensation intact to all modalities. Gait normal, including tandem, heel and toe walking. Romberg negative.

Impression: recovered from Guillain-Barre syndrome. Persistent areflexia in the legs is common after AIDP and does not by itself mean ongoing disease.

Plan: no further routine neurology visits needed. I have asked him to return promptly, or go to the emergency department, if he develops new weakness, numbness, double vision or unsteadiness.

Neurology

documents.title: Neurology letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tyler, got the letter from your neurologist. Great to see you've made a full recovery. I've moved the GBS to your past history in our chart. If anything new comes up with weakness, numbness, balance or vision, let us know right away.

reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain without contrast. No restricted diffusion. No mass, hemorrhage or extra-axial collection. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. Brainstem and cerebellum normal in signal and volume. No abnormal signal in the white matter. Orbits and extraocular muscles unremarkable on included images. Major intracranial flow voids present.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD (received 07/16/2026)
Date of visit: 07/10/2026

CC: seeing double, can't walk straight

HPI: 29M with Guillain-Barre syndrome last July (AIDP, IVIG), recovered per neurology. Over the past three days he has felt off balance when walking, worse each day; this morning he could not stand up without a friend holding his arm. Along with that his eyes do not move right, especially looking to either side, and things look doubled and blurry. Says he has not been sick lately, but on questioning had a day or two of diarrhea roughly two weeks ago that cleared without treatment. No fever, headache, neck pain, weakness of the arms or legs, numbness, trouble swallowing or breathing. Takes no medications. NKDA.

Family/social: father with controlled hypertension, mother hypothyroid; no autoimmune or neuromuscular disease in first-degree relatives. Project coordinator in construction. Never smoker. Drinks 2-3 a week.

Exam: vital signs within normal limits. Alert and oriented, speech normal. Neither eye abducts fully on lateral gaze, consistent with bilateral sixth nerve (lateral rectus) palsies; horizontal diplopia worse at far lateral gaze. Pupils equal and reactive. Face symmetric, palate midline. Strength 5/5 in all extremities. Reflexes absent at knees and ankles. Sensation intact. Finger-to-nose without dysmetria. Gait wide-based, cannot walk heel to toe. Heart, lungs and abdomen normal.

ED course: CBC and BMP normal. MRI brain normal. LP: CSF protein 39 mg/dL, glucose 64 mg/dL, WBC 0, RBC 1. Anti-GQ1b antibody sent. Neurology consulted.

Impression: recurrent Guillain-Barre syndrome, presentation suggestive of the Miller Fisher variant (ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, areflexia).
Disposition: admitted to neurology for observation.

events.reason: Recurrent Guillain-Barre syndrome, Miller Fisher variant

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Neurology Discharge Summary
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - Neurology (received 07/16/2026)
Admitted 07/10/2026 (observation), discharged 07/13/2026

Diagnosis: Guillain-Barre syndrome, recurrent, Miller Fisher variant. Anti-GQ1b antibody positive (resulted 07/13).
Prior: Guillain-Barre syndrome (AIDP) July 2025, treated with IVIG, fully recovered.
Allergies: NKDA.

Course: admitted for neuro checks and respiratory monitoring. FVC and NIF every 8 hours, all normal. Bedside swallow screen passed. Limb strength full throughout the stay. Lateral gaze limitation and gait unsteadiness stable through 07/12, slightly better by discharge. MRI brain and CSF in the ED were normal; see ED record. Anti-GQ1b positive, which fits the clinical picture.

Treatment: supportive care only. The Miller Fisher variant is usually self-limited, and with full strength and normal respiratory function we agreed with the patient not to give IVIG this time.

PT: safe for discharge home walking with a single-point cane.

Discharge medications: none.
Instructions: no driving while double vision persists. Outpatient physical therapy referral sent. Neurology clinic in about 4 weeks. See PCP within 1-2 weeks. Return for limb weakness, trouble swallowing or breathing, or worsening vision or balance.
Work: off until cleared by neurology.

documents.title: Back in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey, I'm in the hospital again. Different this time, it's my eyes and balance, my legs are strong. They think it's another GBS, a type called Miller Fisher. MRI was fine. Just keeping you in the loop.

documents.title: RE: Back in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Tyler, sorry to hear it, and thank you for the heads up. Good that your strength and breathing are holding. Let the team know right away if your swallowing, breathing or strength changes. Once you're home our nurse will call to set up a visit.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Phone Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Spoke with pt, home since yesterday afternoon after 3-night neurology stay. Using the cane, a friend is checking in on him in the evenings. Double vision still there when he looks to the side, better straight ahead. Not driving. No trouble swallowing, breathing OK, arms and legs feel strong. No new prescriptions.

Requested ED record and discharge summary from the hospital. Booked with PCP Tue 7/21 10:40. Pt knows to call 911 or go to ED for breathing/swallowing trouble or new weakness.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up.

29M, history of GBS (AIDP) July 2025 treated with IVIG, recovered by January. Admitted 7/10-7/13 with 3 days of diplopia and gait ataxia. Bilateral lateral rectus palsies, areflexia in the legs, full strength. MRI brain normal, CSF normal (protein 39, no cells). Anti-GQ1b positive. Diagnosed as recurrent GBS, Miller Fisher variant. Supportive care, no IVIG. Records received 7/16 and reviewed.

Today: double vision is gone when looking straight ahead, still there on looking left or right. Walking with the cane outdoors, holds furniture at home. No falls. No arm or leg weakness, no numbness, swallowing and breathing fine. Not driving; friends and coworkers giving him rides. PT starts next week. Frustrated that it happened again but coping.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: vitals normal. Pupils equal and reactive. Abduction limited in both eyes, diplopia on lateral gaze, normal in primary gaze. Face symmetric. Strength 5/5 in all four limbs. Reflexes absent at knees and ankles. Sensation intact. Gait wide-based with cane, unable to tandem.

A/P
1. Recurrent Guillain-Barre syndrome, Miller Fisher variant, improving. Outpatient PT. Neurology follow-up in August. No driving until neurology clears it. Reviewed red flags.
2. Work: out of work note until neurology visit.

Follow-up with me in about two months, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Work Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:

Tyler Griffin was hospitalized July 10-13, 2026 and remains under treatment. He is unable to work at this time. He will be re-evaluated by his specialist in August, and an updated note will follow.

events.reason: Follow-up, Miller Fisher variant of Guillain-Barre syndrome

documents.title: Neurology Clinic Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology outpatient clinic
Visit date: 08/11/2026

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Griffin a month after his admission for a recurrence of Guillain-Barre syndrome, this time the Miller Fisher variant (anti-GQ1b positive), managed supportively. His AIDP episode in July 2025 recovered fully after IVIG.

He is steadily better. He sees double now only when looking all the way to one side. Stopped using the cane last week. In PT twice weekly. No limb weakness, numbness, swallowing or breathing symptoms. No medications.

Exam: mild limitation of abduction in both eyes, diplopia only at far lateral gaze. Other cranial nerves normal. Strength 5/5. Reflexes absent in the legs. Sensation intact. Gait close to normal without a device; still unsteady with tandem walking.

Impression: Miller Fisher variant of Guillain-Barre syndrome, recovering. I expect full recovery over the coming weeks to months.

Plan:
- May return to office duties from 08/24/2026. No job-site work for now.
- No driving until I clear him, once the double vision has resolved.
- Continue PT.
- Neurology follow-up in October.

Neurology
